column4:
My primary materials are silk + elemental forces. The core components of my work are: body + space + presence.

Exploring silk in relation to architecture reveals material and environmental dualities: light and shadow, tension and flow, gravity and weightlessness. By investigating dualities within inhabited space, I employ form as social metaphor, questioning dynamics of power, restraint, and release.

Silk transforms through dyeing processes and entropic conditions. I move from intentional binding and dyeing toward surrender to the unknown, as pigment creates unpredictable patterns.

Varying degrees of tension or flow interrupt or embody the movement inherent in the material. Stillness and ephemerality bring awareness to time and the present moment. The viewer-participant engages the work physically and sensually/somatically through movement. Drawing from a lineage of feminine mystics across cultures, I invite a direct encounter with body and space, where liberation is experienced in the here and now.

ZØ is a contemporary multidisciplinary artist working at the intersection of sound, visual art, fashion, and creative technology. Based in New York City, she operates through her studio entity StuDiØ ZØ, which she founded and runs as a single-member creative practice.
Across her six primary disciplines — DJing, music production, painting, fashion design, creative technology, and AI architecture — ZØ treats each medium as part of a single integrated ecosystem rather than as a separate career. DJ sets feed into generative paintings; paintings inform fashion silhouettes; fashion shapes live event design; events return to the music. This integrated approach is what she calls Ancient Futurism — a creative philosophy fusing monumental ancient aesthetics (temple geometry, sacred symbology, ritual form) with parametric design, generative art systems, and AI-native production tools.

Randall Junyu Xiao (肖俊宇) (b. Shenzhen, China) is an editorial and commercial photographer based in New York City, specializing in sports and entertainment. His work has been commissioned by brands including Nike, Adidas, On, Bandit, OPPO/Hasselblad, MLB, and NBA, and publications like National Geographic and ESPN. He moved to Buffalo, New York at fourteen, an experience that first drew him into American sports culture and, in turn, into photography. He is a graduate of the University of Michigan.

A master of slow shutter in fast moving events, Xiao approaches photography the way a musician approaches an instrument. He treats composition, technique, and color as a working vocabulary, learned deeply enough to be played with rather than followed. Much like a jazz musician improvising within a structure, his images favor a strong sense of play and spontaneity. This sensibility informs both his editorial work and his personal practice, where he continues to explore the space between commercial precision and creative freedom.
